share.start.allH: Everything a share can hold, for this realm only. It can add and delete computers and projects, run commands inside computers (anything on them, secrets included, is reachable this way), see their logs and environment values, add SSH keys that keep working after the share ends, and change their features and network settings. Program addresses, storage shares and Bot links it sets up can let other people in, and keep working after you stop the share. It can add computers and turn on AI and Hoody Kit, which cost money. It still leaves out your billing and wallet, your vault, your email and account history, your sign-in history, and your staff tools. Until an update ships, it can also see your project invitations and the people in your projects.

faq.secretOnce.q: Can I see a key's secret again?
faq.secretOnce.a: No. A key's secret is shown once, when the key is made, so copy it then. When you close that panel, the secret is gone and can't be shown again from this panel. Lost one? Delete it and make a new one. For the same access with a new secret, copy the key: the copy has the same rights, realms and addresses, and the original keeps working.
faq.whatIsKey.q: What is an API key for?
faq.whatIsKey.a: A key lets your agent, the CLI or the SDK act for you. Give each one its own key, with an end date. Name it after the agent or app that uses it; a name takes letters, digits, spaces, _ and -. Use the secret as HOODY_TOKEN in the SDK and HTTP examples.
faq.realms.q: Which realms does a key work in?
faq.realms.a: You choose when you make it. All realms: everything on your account, now and later. Pick realms: only the realms you tick, and the key works only on those realms' addresses. A key made while one realm is selected works only in that realm and cannot see or change anything in other realms; to make one for several realms or all of them, switch to All realms first. A key limited to realms can't be widened to all realms later: make a new key for that.
faq.rights.q: What can a key do, and what does Full mean?
faq.rights.a: Full, or only the rights you tick. Start from ticks the rights of a ready-made set, and you can change them before you make the key. Full uses the server's full access set with its defaults, so vault access stays off. The help text under Full is a summary, not a list of every right: one version leaves out billing and sign-in settings, the other says billing and payments are included. When the list of rights can't be read, what Full covers is unknown, and the help text shows the billing version. A key can be allowed to make other keys; a key it makes never gets more than it has itself.
faq.endsAndAddresses.q: When does a key stop working, and can I limit where it works from?
faq.endsAndAddresses.a: You set an end: Never, 90 days, 1 year or a date. On a date, the key stops at the start of that day, UTC. You can also list the IPv4 addresses or ranges it may be used from, comma separated, such as 203.0.113.7 or 198.51.100.0/24. Leave the list empty and the key works from anywhere. Changing what a key can do, where, or until when may ask for your 2FA code.
faq.sshKey.q: How does the SSH key work?
faq.sshKey.a: An SSH key belongs to one computer: each computer holds one key, and a key another computer already uses can't be added again. Pick the computer in the top bar. Paste your public key, the .pub file (for example id_ed25519.pub); never paste a private key. A public key starts with ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa-sha2-. Once you remove it, whoever holds the matching private key can no longer log in to that computer with ssh.
faq.shareRealm.q: What does sharing a realm give someone?
faq.shareRealm.a: Access to every computer in the realm, including computers added later, for a set time and with the rights you choose. To share only some computers, put them in a new realm and share that. A share never holds money rights, your email or history, your vault, your sign-in history, or keys of its own. Its key stops working when the share ends or you stop it; program addresses they saved can keep working after that.
faq.shareMessage.q: What do I send to the person I share with?
faq.shareMessage.a: The short message you get when the share is made. It is shown only once, so copy it. A sign-in link, when there is one, fills in their sign-in on this Hub; they see what it opens and press Open themselves. With Include the token off, the QR code, when available, opens this Hub and they paste your message there; the agent prompt, when available, has a placeholder where the token goes. On, the QR code can hold the token too, so keep it as safe as the message. The agent prompt is for pasting into an agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, so it can work in this realm.
nk.realmsMore: Which realms can a key work in?
nk.realmsWhy: All realms covers your whole account, now and later. A key limited to realms works only in the ones ticked and can't be widened later.
nk.rightsWhy: Full gives the key the full access set, with vault access off. Choose rights sends only the rights ticked; Start from only ticks a ready-made set.
share.sendMoreA: The message. It is shown only once, so copy it and send it the way you would send a password.
